incidents.vector: Ransomware-as-a-service operation breaching victims via edge-device exploitation (FortiOS, Erlang/OTP SSH, Windows SMB and other CVEs), stolen credentials and initial-access brokers, then deploying a custom Go backdoor and an EDR-killer framework.
incidents.impact: A fast-growing RaaS crew claimed 580 victims across 77 countries since inception and became the second most active ransomware operation of 2026, peaking at 117 claimed victims in June while offering affiliates an unusually high 90% payout.

incidents.vector: A CISA contractor committed privileged Amazon AWS GovCloud access keys to a public GitHub repository, exposing sensitive credentials.
incidents.impact: CISA pulled the repo, revoked access and rotated all secrets; forensic log analysis found no external misuse of the keys and no customer or mission data exposed, but the leak drew congressional scrutiny.

incidents.vector: China-linked operators planted malware disguised as a portal update on the Balochistan Police complaint-management system, infecting officers and citizens who used the site; a parallel India-linked cluster used lure documents against the same networks.
incidents.impact: Compromised criminal records, biometric and fingerprint data, personnel files and citizen complaints; assessed as tied to protecting Chinese nationals working on the China-Pakistan Economic Corridor, with a separate India-nexus campaign hitting the same target.

incidents.victim: Five US companies (nonprofit, financial services, hospitality, healthcare)
incidents.vector: A ransomware-negotiation insider fed victims' confidential negotiating positions and cyber-insurance limits to ransomware affiliates and separately helped deploy the ransomware, maximizing extortion demands.
incidents.impact: The insider was sentenced to 70 months; the scheme extorted a combined $75.3M from five victims (individual ransoms up to ~$26.8M), with $10M in assets seized and two co-conspirators also sentenced.

incidents.vector: A Dutch-speaking man posing as an Odido IT employee phoned customer service and social-engineered staff into granting access to a customer contact system, enabling bulk download of customer records.
incidents.impact: Personal data of more than 6 million customers was exposed; Dutch police took the group's data-distribution servers offline and are pursuing a local accomplice.

incidents.victim: Unpatched Ruckus and ASUS edge routers (proxy-network nodes)
incidents.vector: Exploiting known n-day vulnerabilities in unpatched Ruckus wireless and ASUS AiCloud routers to deploy custom malware and enroll the devices into an operational relay box (ORB) proxy network.
incidents.impact: Cisco Talos found the actor expanding a covert 'LapDogs' proxy network with new malware families, building infrastructure that other China-nexus espionage groups use to mask attacks on high-value targets.

incidents.victim: Consumers and small businesses in the US and EU
incidents.vector: Malvertising lured victims to fake cracked-software download pages serving a Go loader (fraudulent code-signing certificate, file-inflation and AMSI-bypass tricks) that drops an information stealer and a Monero cryptominer.
incidents.impact: The campaign, spiking in April 2026, stole browser credentials, cookies and crypto wallets while mining Monero on victim machines; Unit 42 identified 43 loader binaries sharing a toolchain with a concurrent stealer campaign.

incidents.victim: Oracle PeopleSoft customers (Nissan North America, AdaptHealth, education sector)
incidents.vector: Mass exploitation of an Oracle PeopleSoft zero-day vulnerability to access application infrastructure, exfiltrate data and extort victims.
incidents.impact: An extortion crew's exploitation of a PeopleSoft zero-day drove disclosed breaches at Nissan North America and medical-equipment maker AdaptHealth (patient data accessed, SEC notified) and an active compromise campaign against education-sector deployments.

incidents.vector: Hacktivists breached the company and ran a destructive wiper operation across its infrastructure.
incidents.impact: Attackers claim they wiped roughly 3,000 servers and workstations and 700 virtual machines, deleted all backups and stole more than 650 TB of documents in a May 2026 breach disclosed in early July.

incidents.victim: Former Member of the European Parliament (spyware-committee member)
incidents.vector: The MEP's phone was repeatedly infected with NSO Group's Pegasus commercial spyware while he sat on the parliamentary committee investigating spyware abuses.
incidents.impact: Citizen Lab identified repeated Pegasus infections during 2022-2023 while the committee was active; the operator was not attributed.

incidents.victim: Embedded and industrial devices using the FatFs filesystem driver
incidents.vector: Seven newly disclosed memory-corruption bugs in the widely used FatFs driver let a crafted filesystem image on removable media (or via some over-the-air update paths) execute code and jailbreak a device.
incidents.impact: Tens of millions of devices across dozens of independent codebases are potentially affected with no patches available; exploitation requires physical access or auto-mounting update scenarios, and remediation is expected to take years.

incidents.vector: A newly launched ransomware operation breached the telco and is extorting it.
incidents.impact: The operator says its mobile-payments platform was not affected; Taiwan's Ministry of Digital Affairs opened an investigation into whether personal data was stolen.

incidents.vector: The North American division disclosed a security breach; the intrusion vector was not specified.
incidents.impact: A March-April 2026 incident exposed employee information; no group has claimed responsibility.

incidents.victim: Home internet users worldwide (smart TVs, streaming and set-top boxes)
incidents.vector: Operators distributed malicious proxy SDKs bundled into home devices and hidden in downloadable apps to conscript over 2 million devices as residential-proxy exit nodes rented out to criminals.
incidents.impact: Google, with the FBI, IRS Criminal Investigation and Lumen, disrupted and seized the NetNut/Popa residential proxy network, degrading it by millions of devices; the network had been used by 316 distinct threat clusters (criminal and espionage) for IP obfuscation and password-spray attacks.

incidents.victim: Microsoft 365 tenants (including a US life-sciences firm)
incidents.vector: Device-code phishing abusing Microsoft's OAuth 2.0 device authorization grant to bypass MFA, delivered via vendor-impersonation invoice lures and look-alike SharePoint tenants, then escalating to primary refresh token persistence.
incidents.impact: Talos uncovered a phishing-as-a-service panel with 80+ API endpoints for token capture, MFA-surviving persistence, business-email-compromise and cloud-storage exfiltration; observed lures spoofed a contractor to target a US life-sciences firm's accounts-payable staff.

incidents.victim: 15 open-source software projects (Linux kernel, FFmpeg, 7-Zip, PHP, VLC, OpenVPN and others)
incidents.vector: A researcher used an AI model to fuzz code and published proof-of-concept exploits and write-ups for more than a dozen zero-day vulnerabilities across 15 open-source projects without notifying vendors.
incidents.impact: Unpatched zero-days affecting widely used software were publicly disclosed; nine have received CVE IDs so far and several projects are rushing patches.

incidents.victim: Department of Homeland Security — Homeland Security Information Network (HSIN)
incidents.vector: Intruders breached the HSIN network used to share sensitive data with federal, state, local and industry partners, along with a connected SharePoint system.
incidents.impact: A sensitive government information-sharing network was compromised between late May and early June; the identity of the intruders and the data taken remain unknown.

incidents.vector: The US insurance sector's standards body was breached; the intrusion vector was not disclosed.
incidents.impact: NAIC suspended insurer risk designations and some credit-rating agencies paused data sharing to avoid exposing sensitive information; NAIC says it has evicted the attackers and is restoring operations.

incidents.vector: Hackers stole customer data from the insurer's Japanese operations; the vector was not specified.
incidents.impact: More than 4.38 million customers were impacted, following a separate breach disclosure the prior year.

incidents.vector: A ransomware group breached the central bank's network and later leaked stolen files.
incidents.impact: Files allegedly taken from the central bank were leaked on the dark web; Libyan authorities are investigating a breach traced to an incident weeks earlier.

incidents.vector: A new ransomware group attacked the company, forcing it to take its entire IT network offline.
incidents.impact: Nidec took its whole IT network offline amid a $2M ransom demand; the firm was also hit by ransomware in late 2024.

incidents.vector: A data-extortion group breached the law firm; the vector was not specified.
incidents.impact: The firm was breached in May 2026 and refused to pay the ransom.

incidents.vector: A data-extortion group breached the manufacturer and exfiltrated internal documents.
incidents.impact: Roughly 200,000 documents were leaked after the company refused to pay, including images of the upcoming iPhone 18 and its components.

incidents.attacker: Iran — military and IRGC (Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps)
incidents.vector: State-linked Iranian cyberattacks targeting Israeli organizations across multiple sectors.
incidents.impact: Iranian cyberattacks on Israel tripled year-over-year, with Israel's National Cyber Directorate investigating 4,800 incidents in June versus 1,600 a year earlier, most traced to Iran's military and IRGC.

incidents.victim: Users of AI coding assistants and impersonated brands
incidents.vector: 'Phantom squatting' — adversaries pre-register web domains that large language models consistently hallucinate for legitimate brands, then serve phishing kits to traffic that AI systems route to those domains.
incidents.impact: Unit 42 confirmed the technique is active in the wild across multiple sectors, including a case where an attacker used an AI coding assistant to stage a phishing kit on a hallucinated domain the firm had flagged weeks earlier.

incidents.victim: North American academic, medical and military research community
incidents.vector: A sophisticated cross-sector espionage campaign targeting research organizations that went undetected for more than a year.
incidents.impact: Google's threat intelligence group attributed a long-running espionage campaign against North American research institutions to a China-nexus actor; the intrusion persisted undetected for over a year.

incidents.victim: Organizations running Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager
incidents.vector: Zero-day exploitation of a Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager vulnerability (CVE-2026-20245) to escalate privileges from a compromised administrative account to root-level access.
incidents.impact: Mandiant identified in-the-wild exploitation of a Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager zero-day enabling attackers to gain root on the management platform.

incidents.victim: Browser users (Edge, Chrome, Firefox extension ecosystem)
incidents.attacker: Criminal gang — fraud and data theft
incidents.vector: 119 malicious browser extensions published across 90+ developer accounts delivered genuine functionality but activated steganography-hidden payloads days after install to steal credentials, backdoor browsers and commit affiliate fraud.
incidents.impact: Microsoft removed 119 malicious Edge extensions tied to a long-running operation; more than 2.6 million users are believed to have downloaded the group's extensions, likely higher across other browsers.

incidents.victim: Klue customers (~20 companies including Huntress, Recorded Future, Snyk, Jamf, Tanium)
incidents.vector: Attackers breached SaaS vendor Klue, stole OAuth tokens from customer accounts and used them to access customers' Salesforce integrations and exfiltrate data.
incidents.impact: The supply-chain breach's victim list grew to close to 20 companies, with sensitive data stolen from customers' Salesforce instances via compromised OAuth tokens.

incidents.vector: Hackers exploited a bug in the platform's web-wallet generation software to steal customer assets.
incidents.impact: More than $2.4 million in customer assets was stolen; the platform entered maintenance mode to replace the software and promised to refund affected users.

incidents.vector: Hacktivists defaced a government web portal in protest.
incidents.impact: A government portal was defaced in protest of Malaysia's planned internet age-verification laws.

incidents.victim: Transport for London (and US healthcare providers SSM Health and Sutter Health)
incidents.vector: SIM-swapping and voice/SMS phishing to steal employee credentials and MFA one-time codes, enabling network intrusion and extortion.
incidents.impact: Two members of an English-speaking extortion crew pleaded guilty in the UK to the 2024 cyberattack that crippled Transport for London; one also admitted conspiring to hack US healthcare providers, with a related US case tying the group to 120 intrusions and $115M in ransom payments.

incidents.vector: A cyberattack on a medical-billing provider that services most German university hospitals (vector not disclosed).
incidents.impact: A March 2026 attack led to theft of sensitive health data for tens of thousands of patients, with a large supply-chain blast radius; cited in a first-half 2026 healthcare trend report.

incidents.vector: A ransomware attack on the hospital network (initial vector not disclosed).
incidents.impact: A February 2026 ransomware attack disrupted operations for more than two weeks and forced a shutdown of network access across all 35 facilities; cited in a first-half 2026 healthcare ransomware trend report.

incidents.vector: A data breach at the third-party healthcare service provider (vector not disclosed).
incidents.impact: Disclosed in February 2026, the breach affected 3.4 million patients at customer facilities; cited in a first-half 2026 healthcare trend report.
